title: Purpose of the Document
text:
This document defines the updated proposed solution for the VECV PQMP Case Tracking
Mobile Application.
The document captures:
1. Business scope.
2. User journeys.
3. Functional modules.
4. Case lifecycle.
5. Integration requirements.
6. Order and part status visibility.
7. Case assignment and backend handling.
8. Customer feedback.
9. Invoice/barcode scan-assisted capture.
10. Consignment tracking.
11. Data handling rules.
12. Audit requirements.
13. Reports and dashboards.
14. Non-functional requirements.
15. Risks, dependencies, open points, and out-of-scope items.

title: Background
text:
The PQMP / EGP ecosystem is used for handling cases related to:
1. Order status.
2. Expected delivery updates.
3. Order cancellation.
4. Norms modification.
5. Delivery concerns.
6. Invoice-related queries.
7. Pending part concerns.
8. Other support-related issues.
In the current process, users receive case references and updates through available
communication channels. However, the complete case journey, current case owner, latest
status, part-wise order position, pending quantity, expected delivery date, delivery progress, and
closure remarks will be always available in a simple and mobile-friendly view. The proposed
solution aims to provide a clear case tracking experience where users can create cases, track
progress, view timelines, check order-related details, review part-wise delivery
information, receive notifications, access closure remarks , simple customer feedback,
scan-assisted order/part capture, possible consignment tracking from a single


portal/mobile interface.

title: Business Objectives
text:
The key business objectives of the proposed solution are:
1. Provide a structured and easy-to-use case creation experience through mobile.
2. Enable users to track all their cases from a single My Cases view.
3. Show current case status, latest update, timeline, owner/team information where
permitted, feedbacks and closure remarks.
4. Reduce manual follow-ups by making case progress visible to users.
5. Display order-level details for order-related cases.
6. Display part-wise quantity and delivery position wherever order data is available.
7. Show pending quantity and expected delivery information in a user-friendly format.
8. Prevent confusion by avoiding raw backend values such as technical codes, blank
dates, null values, or invalid date formats.
9. Support notifications for key events such as case creation, assignment, status update,
clarification, order update, closure, and reopening.
10. Provide dashboard and customer analytics in the current phase.
11. Capture simple customer feedback against the case ID.
12. Support scan-assisted capture from invoice/barcode where available.
13. Support consignment tracking where third-party logistics API is available.
14. Create a scalable foundation for future enhancements, deeper integrations, additional
case categories, and extended user roles.

title: Scope Principles
text:
The proposed solution will follow these principles:
1. The user experience should remain simple, business-readable, and mobile-friendly.
2. Case creation will be handled through structured portal/mobile forms.
3. Dashboard and customer analytics will remain part of the current phase.
4. Order and part status details will be shown only for applicable order-related cases.
5. Invoice/barcode scan will assist capture, but the user must review/select relevant part
details before case submission.
6. Consignment tracking will depend on logistics API availability.
7. User access will be controlled through role, user, dealer, location and mapping rules in
existing PQMP web portal.
8. All existing business rules, field mappings, integrations, notification channels, status
mappings, assignment logic, closure rules, and dashboard KPIs that are already
applicable in the existing web portal will continue to be followed for the mobile app. Any
new feature, enhancement, change in logic, or additional functionality will require
confirmation and approval from VECV before inclusion in the final scope of work
document.

title: Current Process Summary
text:
The current case management process involves case creation in PQMP / EGP web portal,
assignment to the relevant support team, review of case details, order-related checking in ECC /
SAP where applicable, update sharing, and case closure.
For order-related cases, the support team needs to check order number, PO number, part
number, delivered quantity, pending quantity, invoice reference, delivery reference, and
expected delivery date from ECC / SAP or related backend sources.

title: Current High-Level Workflow
text:
1. User raises a case related to order, part, delivery, invoice, cancellation, norms, or
another issue.
2. System generates a case number.
3. Case registration confirmation is sent through the available channel.


4. Case appears in the PQMP / EGP case listings.
5. Case is assigned to the relevant owner or support team as per case assignment matrix.
6. Support team reviews issue, category, documents, and related details.
7. For order-related cases, order and part details are checked from ECC / SAP or the
relevant backend source.
8. Support team updates case status and remarks.
9. Customers/ Dealers receive updates through the available communication channel.
10. Case is resolved and closed after the required action or response.

title: Current Challenges
text:
The following challenges are identified:
1. Users don’t have clear visibility of the current case status.
2. Users don’t know what the next action is.
3. Order and part-related information is not available in a simple mobile-friendly format.
4. Part-wise delivery status not be clearly visible.
5. Pending quantity and expected delivery date require manual follow-up.
6. Backend values such as blank dates, invalid dates, or technical codes create confusion
if shown directly.
7. Case updates depend heavily on manual communication.
8. Attachments, remarks, clarification history, and closure responses are not easily
accessible in one place.
9. Auto closure can create risk if SAP/API data is incorrect or not synchronized.
10. Consignment status is not visible.
11. Email-based case generation requires more discussion before scope finalization.

title: Solution Direction
text:
The proposed portal/mobile solution will address the above challenges by providing:
1. My Cases listing for easy tracking.
2. Case detail page with full case summary.
3. Current status and latest update at the top of the page.
4. Chronological case timeline.
5. Order summary for order-related cases.
6. Part-wise delivery status with ordered, delivered, and pending quantity.
7. Expected delivery / EDA visibility wherever available.
8. Scan-assisted invoice/barcode capture where available.
9. Consignment tracking where logistics API is available.
10. User-friendly handling of missing, invalid, or unavailable backend values.
11. Notifications for key case and order events.
12. Customer feedback capture after case completion.
13. Attachment and comment visibility based on access rights.

title: Solution Summary
text:
The proposed PQMP Mobile Case Tracking Solution will act as a single digital window for users
to create, view, and track cases.
Users will be able to:
1. Log in securely.
2. View dashboard and case analytics.
3. Create a new case through a structured form.
4. Track existing cases from My Cases.
5. Open case details and view latest status.
6. View order-level information for order-related cases.
7. View part-wise delivery status and pending quantity.
8. Use invoice/barcode scan-assisted capture where available.
9. View consignment tracking where logistics data is available.
10. Upload and view attachments.
11. Add comments or clarifications where permitted.
12. Receive notifications on important case events.
13. View final closure remarks once the case is closed.
14. Provide simple feedback/rating after case completion.

title: Proposed User Journey
text:
1. User logs in using the approved authentication method.
2. System validates the user and applies role/data access mapping.
3. User lands on the dashboard.
4. Dashboard displays case summary, recent updates, and quick actions.
5. User can either create a new case or open My Cases.
6. While creating a case, user selects category and sub-category.
7. System displays relevant fields based on selected category.
8. User enters case details, remarks, order/PO/part details where applicable, and uploads
attachments if required.
9. Where applicable, user scans invoice/barcode to capture available details.
10. System displays scanned details for review.
11. User selects relevant part/parts for which the case is being raised.
12. System validates the entered information.
13. System creates the case in PQMP / EGP and returns the case number.
14. Case becomes visible under My Cases.


15. Backend system assigns the case to the relevant support desk based on case
assignment matrix.
16. For order-related cases, system fetches or displays ECC / SAP-linked details where
integration is available.
17. User opens the case detail page to see status, timeline, order status, part-wise status,
comments, attachments, consignment status where available, and closure response.
18. Notifications are sent for important updates.
19. Case is resolved and closed with final remarks.
20. User provides feedback/rating where enabled.

title: Key Business Benefits
text:
1. Improved visibility of case progress.
2. Reduced manual follow-up between users and support teams.
3. Clear order-level and part-level information for order-related cases.
4. Better user confidence through latest update and timeline visibility.
5. Reduced confusion by converting backend values into simple business labels.
6. Better support governance through status tracking, ownership, audit, and escalation
visibility.
7. Better workload management through balanced support desk assignment.
8. Improved customer experience through a single customer-facing support identity.
9. Faster case creation through scan-assisted capture where available.
10. Better service quality tracking through customer feedback.
11. Improved closure governance through review-based closure handling.
12. Scalable structure for future case categories, reports, integrations, and role expansion.

title: Solution Boundaries
text:
The current solution will include structured mobile case creation and tracking.
Current phase will include dashboard/customer analytics and core case tracking. Separate
escalation management portal integration and approval workflow are parked for Phase 2 as per


discussion.

title: Dealer / Customer User
text:
This is the primary user of the portal/mobile case tracking solution.
The user will be able to:
1. Log in to the system.
2. View dashboard summary.
3. Create a new case.
4. View own or mapped cases.
5. Track case progress.
6. View order and part status where applicable.
7. Scan invoice/barcode where supported.
8. View consignment status where available.
9. Upload attachments.
10. Add comments or clarification responses where allowed.
11. Receive notifications.
12. View closure remarks.
13. Provide feedback/rating after case completion.

title: Customer-Facing Support Persona
text:
A single external customer-facing support persona should be shown to the user.
The customer should not see backend labels such as:
1. EGP Desk 1.
2. EGP Desk 1.
3. EGP Desk 3.
4. Internal support desk user names, unless approved.
Expected behavior:
1. Customer raises the case through one common support interface.
2. Customer tracks the case through one case ID.
3. Customer receives updates through one customer-facing support identity.
4. Backend assignment remains internal.
5. Internal desk transfer should not create confusion for the customer.
6. Technical discussions with VECV would be required.

title: PQMP / EGP Support User
text:
Support users will handle cases through the existing support process or approved access route.
Support users be able to:
1. View assigned cases.
2. Review case details.
3. Add remarks or updates.
4. Update case status where permitted.
5. View order and part details where required.
6. Check SAP/ECC details where needed.
7. Respond to clarification requests.
8. Upload supporting details.
9. Close or resolve cases as per workflow.
10. Receive cases through balanced assignment.
11. Receive transferred cases from admin.
Mobile access for support users should be enabled only if approved by VECV.

title: Admin / Configuration User
text:
Admin users will manage configuration, master data, and backend assignment controls where
applicable.
Admin users manage:
1. Case categories.
2. Case sub-categories.

4. Status mapping.
5. Part status rules.
6. Notification templates.
7. Attachment policy.
8. User/dealer/location mappings.
9. Priority values.

title: System / Integration Layer
text:
The system/integration layer is not a human user, but it is required for solution execution.
It will support:
1. Case creation and retrieval from PQMP / EGP.
2. Order and part data fetch from ECC / SAP.
3. Authentication and session validation.
4. Notification triggering.
5. Attachment handling.
6. Scan-assisted data capture from invoice/barcode.
7. Consignment tracking integration where API is available.
8. Assignment rule execution.
9. Audit logging.
10. Error handling and system monitoring.

title: Role and Access Rules
text:
The system will follow role-based and data-level access control:
1. Users will see only those cases that are created by them or mapped to their authorized
dealer code
2. Users will not be allowed to view cases outside their permitted scope.
3. Customers will not see internal support desk labels unless explicitly approved.
4. Attachments and comments will be visible only as per access policy.


5. Internal support remarks will not be shown to case creators unless marked as user-
facing.
6. Admin/configuration access will be restricted to authorized users only.
7. Management reports will respect hierarchy, dealer, location, region, category, and role-
level visibility.
8. Access control must be enforced at backend level and not only through the user
interface.
9. Unauthorized users must receive a clear message and must not be able to access
restricted data.
10. Admin assignment and transfer rights must be configurable or controlled by role.
11. Feedback visibility must be role-controlled.

title: Overall Flow
text:
1. User logs in to the mobile application.
2. System authenticates the user and loads permitted access.
3. User lands on the dashboard.
4. User selects My Cases or Create Case.
5. For new case creation, user selects category and sub-category.
6. System displays required fields based on selected category.
7. User enters case details, issue description, remarks, order/PO/part information where
applicable, and uploads attachments.
8. User scan invoice/barcode where applicable.
9. System extracts available details from the scan and displays them for user review.
10. User selects relevant part/parts where scan data contains multiple parts.
11. System validates the information.
12. System creates the case in PQMP / EGP.
13. Case number is generated or returned by the backend system.
14. Case appears in My Cases.
15. Case is assigned to the relevant owner/team/support desk based on confirmed
assignment logic.
16. Case moves through review, progress, clarification, resolution, and closure stages as
applicable.
17. For order-related cases, system fetches order and part details from ECC / SAP or
approved backend source.
18. User views order summary and part-wise delivery status.
19. User views consignment status where API is available.
20. User receives notifications for important updates.
21. Case is closed after resolution or based on approved closure rule.
22. User views closure remarks and final status.
23. User submits feedback/rating where enabled.

title: Case Creation Flow
text:
1. User opens Create Case.
2. User selects case category.
3. User selects sub-category.
4. System displays relevant fields.
5. User enters issue title and issue description.
6. User enters contact details and preferred contact mode where required.
7. For order-related cases, user enters order number, PO number, part number, invoice
number, delivery number, chassis number, plant, or quantity details where applicable.
8. User scans invoice/barcode where supported.
9. System reads available invoice/order/part data.
10. User reviews scanned data.
11. User selects applicable part/parts for which the case needs to be created.
12. User corrects or enters missing details manually where required.
13. User uploads supporting documents if required.
14. System validates mandatory fields, format rules, and attachment policy.
15. System creates the case in PQMP / EGP.
16. System displays success confirmation with case number.
17. System triggers notification as per configured event rules.

title: Case Assignment Flow
text:
1. After case creation, the case is assigned to the relevant support team or owner.
2. Assignment happen through existing PQMP / EGP case assignment matrix
3. If Desk 1 has more pending cases and Desk 2 has fewer pending cases, new cases
should be routed toward the lower-load desk until distribution becomes balanced.
4. Admin should be able to assign or transfer cases manually.
5. Customer see a generic support identity but not internal desk allocation.
6. If assignment is pending, the case show a status such as Submitted or Awaiting
Assignment, based on final status mapping.
7. Final rules for assignment, reassignment and rerouting logics need to be
discussed with VECV.

title: Case Processing Flow
text:
The case move through the following status:
1. Assigned - Case is assigned to the relevant team and is being reviewed.
2. Escalated - Case is created and escalated to higher level
3. In Progress - Support team is actively working on the case.
4. Hold - Due to the valid reason the ticket has been put on hold.
5. Inprogress - If the ticket resolution is in active state then it is put in progress status
6. New - Case which are not yet assigned to the owner are generally in this status
7. Reassigned - If the owner of the case changes then case show s the mentioned status.


8. Resume - Support team provides the required response or resolution.
9. Close - Case is completed and closed.
10. Reopened - Case is reopened for further review, if allowed by business rules.

title: ECC / SAP Order Tracking Flow
text:
1. System identifies the type of the case & it’s sub type.
2. System checks whether required order/PO/part reference is available.
3. System fetches or receives order-level and part-level data from ECC / SAP or approved
backend source.
4. System validates quantities, status consistency, dates, and data availability.
5. System maps backend values into user-friendly display labels.
6. System displays order summary and part-wise status.
7. System shows Last Refreshed On timestamp for backend data.
8. If data is unavailable, system displays a clear fallback message.
9. Technical errors are logged internally and not shown directly to the user.
10. If SAP/API data mismatch is identified, the case is marked for review instead of showing
misleading information.

title: Invoice / Barcode Scan Flow
text:
1. User can selects scan option during case creation or order capture.
2. User scans the invoice/barcode.
3. System captures available values such as invoice number, GST number, seller GST
details, HSN code, invoice reference number, and part details where available.
4. System displays extracted values for user review.
5. User selects the part/parts for which the case is being created.
6. User enters missing details manually if scan output is incomplete.
7. System validates final details before case submission.
8. Scan failure should not block case creation if manual entry is possible.

title: Consignment Tracking Flow
text:
1. System identifies whether consignment tracking is applicable for the order/part only if it
is related to specific case type
2. System checks required tracking reference.
3. System calls logistics provider API where available.
4. System displays tracking status in user-friendly format.
5. System shows last refreshed timestamp.
6. If tracking data is unavailable, system shows a fallback message.
7. Technical API errors are logged internally.
8. Third - Party APIs will be provided by VECV.

title: Auto Case Registration from Email
text:
Narendra raised a requirement for automatic case generation from emails sent to a specific
email ID.
The expected behaviour discussed was:
● Customer sends an email to a dedicated support email ID.
● System reads the mail body.
● System identifies the customer query/problem statement.
● If part number or order information is available, system captures it.
● If part details are missing or unclear, the case should still be registered.
● EGP Support Desk can then ask the customer/originator for additional information.
● The purpose is to ensure that no customer query remains unattended
Note:- Technical discussion is required before finalizing this as part of scope.

title: Login and Authentication
text:
1. System shall allow only authenticated users to access the portal/mobile application.
2. System shall map the logged-in user to role, dealer/location/user code, and data scope.
3. System shall maintain secure sessions.
4. System shall expire inactive sessions as per approved policy.
5. System shall restrict inactive or unauthorized users.
6. System shall redirect users to the appropriate dashboard based on their role and
access.
7. Final authentication method shall be confirmed by VECV.

title: Dashboard
text:
1. System shall show case summary cards based on user access.
2. Dashboard shall show total cases, open cases, in-progress cases, closed cases, and
recently updated cases.
3. System shall show cases awaiting user response where applicable.
4. Dashboard metrics shall match the data available in case listing.
5. User shall be able to navigate from summary cards to relevant case lists.
6. Customer dashboard shall not expose internal desk allocation.
7. Internal dashboard show support desk workload where access is permitted.
8. Dashboard shall support customer analytics in the current phase.
9. Feedback summary be shown where feedback module is enabled.
10. Closure review count be shown for admin/support users where closure review is
approved.

title: My Cases
text:
1. System shall display only cases created by or mapped to the logged-in user.
2. User shall be able to search by case number and order number.
3. User shall be able to filter cases by status, category, sub-category, priority, date range,
and order-related case type.
4. Each case card shall show case number, category, sub-category, status, priority,
created date, last updated date, order reference, and short description.
5. User shall be able to open full case detail from the listing.
6. User-facing list shall not show internal EGP desk names.
7. Feedback pending cases be indicated after closure/completion.
8. Consignment tracking indicator be shown where applicable.

title: Case Creation
text:
1. System shall provide a structured portal/mobile case creation form.
2. User shall select case category and sub-category.
3. System shall show dynamic fields based on selected category/sub-category.
4. User shall enter issue title, issue description, remarks, contact details, and preferred
contact mode where required.
5. For order-related cases, user shall enter order number, PO number, part number,
invoice number, delivery number, chassis number, plant, or quantity details where
applicable.
6. System shall support invoice/barcode scan-assisted capture where enabled.
7. System shall show scanned values for user review.
8. User shall select relevant part/parts before submission where scanned data contains
multiple parts.


9. System shall validate mandatory fields before submission.
10. System shall validate attachment requirements where applicable.
11. System shall create the case in PQMP / EGP only after successful validation.
12. System shall display the generated or returned case number after successful case
creation.
13. System shall save the case under My Cases after creation.
14. Email-based automatic case creation shall remain an open scope item pending
confirmation.

title: Case Detail
text:
1. System shall show case ID, category, sub-category, current status, priority, assigned
team where permitted, created date, last updated date, and issue details.
2. System shall show the latest update at the top of the case detail page.
3. System shall show case timeline in chronological order.
4. System shall show comments and attachments based on user access.
5. System shall show closure remarks once case is closed.
6. System shall hide sensitive internal information from case creators unless marked as
user-facing.
7. System shall show order and part sections only for applicable order-related cases.
8. System shall show consignment tracking only where data is available.
9. System shall show feedback/rating section after completion/closure where enabled.

title: Order Status
text:
1. System shall show order status section only for order-related cases.
2. System shall display order number, order type, PO number, PO date, dealer/customer,
plant, overall order status, delivered count, pending count, and last refreshed time where
available.
3. System shall show a clear message if order data is not available.
4. System shall not show raw technical backend values to the user.
5. System shall log integration errors internally.
6. System shall mark mismatch cases for review where SAP/API values conflict with case
state.

title: Part-Wise Status
text:
1. System shall display part number, part description, ordered quantity, delivered quantity,
pending quantity, delivery reference, invoice reference, expected date, and part status.


2. System shall calculate pending quantity as ordered quantity minus delivered quantity.
3. If delivered quantity equals ordered quantity, status shall be shown as Fully Delivered.
4. If delivered quantity is greater than zero but less than ordered quantity, status shall be
shown as Partially Delivered.
5. If delivered quantity is zero, status shall be shown as Not Delivered.
6. If backend quantity and status are contradictory, system shall show Under Review and
log the mismatch internally.
7. If expected date is blank, invalid, or unavailable, system shall show Awaiting Update or
Not Available.
8. Consignment tracking be linked at part level where data is available.

title: Comments and Clarifications
text:
1. User shall be able to add comments where case status allows.
2. User shall be able to respond to clarification requests.
3. User shall be able to upload additional attachments where allowed.
4. Reopen request shall require mandatory remarks if reopen is enabled.
5. All comments and clarification actions shall be captured in audit logs.
6. Internal comments shall not be shown to customers unless marked as customer-facing.

title: Notifications
text:
1. System will generate notifications for configured case events.
2. Notifications will be user-specific.
3. Notification message will include case number and business-readable update.
4. Notification shall open the relevant case detail where supported.
5. Failed notifications shall be logged internally.
6. Notification channels shall be finalized by VECV.
7. Feedback notification will be sent after case completion.
8. Consignment update notification be sent where tracking is enabled.

title: Audit and Error Handling
text:
1. System shall record audit logs for case creation, updates, status changes, comments,
attachments, order refresh, notifications, closure, and reopen actions.
2. System shall also record assignment, transfer, scan-assisted capture, feedback,
consignment refresh, and bulk closure actions where applicable.
3. System shall show user-friendly error messages.
4. System shall not show technical errors, raw API responses, stack traces, or database
messages to end users.
5. System shall log technical errors internally with relevant identifiers for troubleshooting.

title: Customer Feedback
text:
1. System shall allow customer feedback after case completion or closure.
2. Feedback shall be linked to the case ID.
3. Rating shall be captured in a simple 1 to 5 format.
4. Remarks field shall be optional.
5. Feedback shall not block closure unless business confirms otherwise.
6. Feedback data shall be available for authorized reporting users.
7. Feedback shall be auditable.

title: Bulk Closure
text:
1. The system already supports manual closure after resolution.
2. System support closure review for fully delivered cases.
3. System support bulk closure after authorized user review.
4. Closure remarks/reason is captured.
5. If SAP/API data indicates delivery but the customer issue is still open, the case is
reviewed before closure.
6. API compatibility needs to be checked.

title: Case Creation Rules
text:
1. Case category is mandatory.
2. Case sub-category is mandatory.
3. Issue description is mandatory.
4. Order/PO details be mandatory for order-related cases.
5. Part number will be mandatory for part-specific cases.
6. Attachments will be mandatory for selected categories.
7. Case number shall be shown only after successful backend case creation.
8. User shall receive a clear success message after case registration.
9. Scanned values must be reviewed before submission.
10. If scanned data contains multiple parts, user must select the relevant part/parts.
11. If scan fails, user proceed with manual entry where allowed.

title: Order and Part Rules
text:
1. Order status section shall appear only for order-related cases.
2. Part-wise status shall appear only where part-level data is available.
3. Pending quantity shall be calculated as ordered quantity minus delivered quantity.
4. Fully delivered status shall require delivered quantity to be equal to ordered quantity.
5. Partially delivered status shall require delivered quantity to be greater than zero and less
than ordered quantity.
6. Not delivered status shall apply when delivered quantity is zero.
7. Status mismatch shall be displayed as Under Review.
8. Backend status codes shall be converted into business-readable labels.
9. Fully delivered cases become eligible for closure review, subject to final rules.

title: Data Display Rules
text:
1. Blank values shall not be shown as blank fields without explanation.
2. Null, undefined, or invalid values shall not be shown to users.
3. Invalid dates such as 0000-00-00 shall be shown as Awaiting Update.
4. Empty quantity shall be shown as Not Available unless the value is confirmed as zero.
5. API timeout shall be shown as Temporarily Unavailable.
6. Unauthorized access shall show a clear no-access message.
7. Customer-facing screens shall not show internal EGP desk names.
8. Last refreshed timestamp shall be shown wherever backend data is displayed.
9. Consignment API failure shall be shown as tracking unavailable, not as a technical error.

title: Closure and Reopen Rules
text:
1. Closure shall require final remarks or resolution response.
2. Closed cases shall remain searchable.
3. Closure date and closure remarks shall be visible to the user.
4. Reopen shall be allowed only if approved by business rules.
5. Reopen request shall require mandatory remarks.
6. Reopen action shall create a timeline and audit entry.

title: Feedback Rules
text:
1. Feedback shall be linked to a case ID.
2. Feedback shall be allowed only after case completion/closure or as per business rule.
3. Rating value shall be simple, such as 1 to 5.
4. Remarks shall be optional.
5. Feedback shall be visible only to authorized users.

title: Case Lifecycle and Status Management
text: Management

title: Recommended Case Statuses
text:
The following statuses are considered:
1. Assigned
2. Escalated
3. In Progress
4. Hold
5. Inprogress
6. New
7. Reassigned Resume
8. Close
9. Reopened

title: Status Transition Rules
text:
1. Draft can move to Submitted after user submits the case.
2. Submitted can move to Awaiting Assignment, Assigned, Under Review, or In Progress.
3. Awaiting Assignment can move to Assigned.
4. Assigned / Under Review can move to In Progress, Clarification Required, Awaiting
Backend Update, Resolved, Closure Pending, or Closed.
5. Clarification Required can move to Awaiting User Response.
6. Awaiting User Response can move to In Progress after user response.
7. Awaiting Backend Update can move to In Progress, Resolved, or Closure Pending after
data is received.
8. Closure Pending can move to Closed after approved closure action.
9. Resolved can move to Closed or Reopened.
10. Closed cases shall not be editable except for reopen where permitted.
11. Reopened cases shall return to review or in-progress stage.

title: Owner Change Rules
text:
1. Every assignment or reassignment shall be recorded.
2. Previous ownership history shall not be overwritten.
3. Current owner/team be shown to the user only where permitted.
4. Internal support desk name should not be shown to customer unless approved.


5. Escalation owner/team shall be logged separately where applicable.
6. If owner information is unavailable, system shall show a user-friendly label such as
Support Team or Under Review.

title: SLA and Ageing Rules
text:
SLA and ageing capability will be supported where required data and rules are available.
The following areas require business confirmation:
1. Case ageing formula.
2. Stage ageing formula.
3. Business calendar and working hours.
4. Priority-wise SLA targets.
5. Hold/pause/resume rule.
6. Escalation thresholds.
7. User-facing SLA display rules.
8. SLA breach visibility.
9. Whether current phase needs only ageing visibility or full SLA workflow.
10. Whether separate escalation management portal integration remains Phase 1.

title: Integration Overview
text:
The solution will require integration with existing systems for case management, order status,
authentication, notification, file storage, master data, scan-assisted capture, and possible
consignment tracking.
The earlier document already included PQMP/EGP, ECC/SAP, authentication, notification, file
storage, and integration error handling as core integration areas.

title: PQMP / EGP Integration
text:
PQMP / EGP integration will support:
1. Case creation.
2. Case list retrieval.
3. Case detail retrieval.
4. Case status retrieval.


5. Timeline retrieval.
6. Remarks and comments retrieval.
7. Attachment references.
8. Closure details.
9. Reopen eligibility, if applicable.
10. Assignment and reassignment events where applicable.
11. Old/pending query handling where approved.

text:
ECC / SAP integration will support order-related data visibility.
Expected data areas include:
1. Order number.
2. Order type.
3. PO number.
4. PO date.
5. Dealer/customer reference.
6. Sold-to party.

9. Part number.

title: Authentication Integration
text:
Authentication be through approved enterprise login, SSO, OTP, user ID/password, or existing
identity provider.
The authentication layer shall provide:
1. User identity.
2. Role information.
3. Dealer/location/user code mapping.


4. Session or token information.
5. Active/inactive user status.

title: Notification Integration
text:
Notification integration support:
1. In-app notification.
2. Push notification.
3. Email notification.
4. SMS notification.
5. WhatsApp notification, if approved.

7. Consignment update notification.

title: File Storage Integration
text:
File storage will support:
1. Attachment upload.
2. Secure file storage.
3. File preview/download.
4. File type validation.
5. File size validation.
6. Access-controlled file links.
7. Retention policy.
8. Attachment audit trail.
9. Invoice/barcode scan image/document reference where applicable.

title: Invoice / Barcode Scan Integration
text:
This integration/capability will support:
1. Barcode/QR/invoice scan.
2. Extraction of available invoice details.
3. Extraction of GST details where available.
4. Extraction of HSN code where available.
5. Extraction of part details where available.
6. User review before submission.
7. Manual correction of scanned data.
8. Failure handling and fallback to manual entry.


Technical team would need below items in order to implement this functionality:
1. Barcode/QR format.
2. Exact fields available.
3. Whether part-level details are always available.
4. Whether OCR is required or only barcode scan is required.
5. Whether scanned values can be edited by user.

title: Consignment Tracking Integration
text:
This integration will support:
1. Logistics provider API connection.
2. Consignment tracking status.
3. Delivery status.
4. Last updated timestamp.
5. Error handling and fallback message.
6. Multi-provider integration in future where required.
Technical team would need below items in order to implement this functionality:
1. Logistics partner list.
2. API documentation.
3. Authentication method.
4. Tracking reference mapping.
5. Refresh frequency.
6. Responsibility for API access and coordination.

title: Integration Error Handling
text:
1. Case detail should remain accessible even if ECC / SAP order data is temporarily
unavailable.
2. User shall see a clear fallback message for unavailable order data.
3. Technical errors shall be logged internally.
4. API response codes and raw error messages shall not be shown to users.
5. Retry and fallback behavior shall be finalized during technical design.
6. Last refreshed timestamp shall be shown wherever backend order/part data is displayed.
7. SAP/API mismatch shall be routed for internal review.
8. Integration failure should be analyzed with the relevant support/technical/SAP IT team.

title: Required Masters and Configurations
text:
The solution require the following masters which will be maintained by the Admin in the existing
web portal.
Master / Configuration Purpose
Case Category Master To define available case categories
Case Sub-Category Master To define sub-categories
Field Configuration Master To control dynamic fields
Status Mapping Master To define case statuses and display labels
Status Transition Configuration To control allowed movement
Part Status Rule Configuration To derive part status from quantity/status
Notification Template Master To configure notification content
Attachment Policy Master To define file rules
User / Dealer / Location Mapping To control data access
Priority Master To define priority values
SLA / Escalation Master If SLA/escalation is included


Integration Mapping To map external fields
Display Label Master To show business-readable labels
Support Desk User Mapping To map backend support users
Assignment Rule Configuration To define balanced assignment rules
Closure Rule Configuration To define manual/bulk/auto closure conditions
Feedback Rating Master To define 1–5 rating values
Logistics Partner Mapping If consignment tracking is enabled

title: Master Governance Rules
text:
1. Only authorized users shall manage master data.
2. Active/inactive flags shall be available for master values.
3. Master changes shall be audited.
4. Existing cases shall not break due to master changes.
5. Backend codes shall be mapped to business-readable labels.
6. Category, sub-category, and dynamic fields shall be centrally configurable.
7. Status mapping shall remain consistent across dashboard, listing, detail, timeline, and
reports.
8. Assignment rules shall be controlled to avoid operational imbalance.
9. Closure rule changes shall be audited due to business impact.
10. Feedback rating scale shall remain simple unless business confirms additional
questions.

title: High-Level Architecture
text:
The solution include the following logical layers:
1. Mobile / Portal Frontend Layer
Provides login, dashboard, case creation, My Cases, case detail, scan capture,
feedback, and notifications.
2. Application / API Layer
Handles business rules, case submission, role access, validation, assignment, timeline,
feedback, and closure handling.
3. Integration Layer
Connects with PQMP / EGP, ECC / SAP, notification gateways, file storage, logistics
APIs, and authentication system.
4. Data and Audit Layer
Stores case references, user mappings, audit logs, attachment metadata, notification
logs, scan metadata, feedback, and integration logs.
5. Admin / Configuration Layer
Manages masters, mappings, assignment rules, notification templates, status rules, and
closure rules.

title: Technical Principles
text:
1. Backend complexity should not be exposed to users.
2. All APIs should return business-readable errors to the app layer.
3. Raw SAP/API errors should be logged internally.
4. Case detail should be available even if order/part data fails temporarily.
5. Last refreshed timestamp should be shown for external data.
6. User-entered data should be preserved where submission fails.
7. Assignment and closure actions should be auditable.


8. Integration failures should be traceable.
9. External logistics APIs should be integrated only after API availability and mapping
confirmation.
10. Email-based case creation should be technically assessed separately before
commitment.

title: Suggested Data Flow
text:
1. User logs in.
2. Authentication validates the user.
3. Role/access mapping is loaded.
4. User creates or views cases.
5. Application layer validates input.
6. Case is created/retrieved from PQMP / EGP.
7. Order and part data is fetched from ECC / SAP where applicable.
8. Scan-assisted data is captured and reviewed where enabled.
9. Consignment data is fetched from logistics API where available.
10. Notifications are triggered for configured events.
11. Audit logs are created for key actions.
12. Reports and dashboards consume authorized data views.
13. Feedback is captured after case completion.

title: Case-Level Data
text:
Case-level data include:
1. Case number.
2. Case category.
3. Case sub-category.
4. Issue title.
5. Issue description.
6. Customer/dealer reference.
7. Created by.
8. Created date.
9. Current status.
10. Latest update.
11. Priority.
12. Assigned team/owner where permitted.
13. Closure remarks.
14. Reopen remarks where applicable.
15. Feedback rating.


16. Feedback remarks.
17. Source channel, if needed.

title: Order-Level Data
text:
Order-level data include:
1. Order number.
2. Order type.
3. PO number.
4. PO date.
5. Dealer/customer reference.
6. Sold-to party.
7. Plant.
8. Chassis number where applicable.
9. Overall order status.
10. Delivered parts.
11. Pending parts.
12. Last refreshed timestamp.
13. Delivery completion flag where available.
14. Consignment reference where available.

title: Part-Level Data
text:
Part-level data include:
1. Part number.
2. Part description.
3. Ordered quantity.
4. Delivered quantity.
5. Pending quantity.
6. Delivery number.
7. Delivery date.
8. Invoice number.
9. Invoice date.
10. Expected delivery / EDA date.
11. Part status.
12. Remarks.
13. HSN code where available from scan.
14. GST/invoice reference where available from scan.
15. Consignment tracking status where available.

title: Audit Trail Requirements
text:
Audit trail shall capture:
1. Case creation.
2. Case update.
3. Status change.
4. Owner/team assignment.
5. Assignment transfer.
6. Comment addition.
7. Attachment upload.
8. Attachment view/download where required.
9. Scan-assisted capture.
10. Order data refresh.
11. Consignment data refresh.
12. Notification trigger.
13. Closure.
14. Bulk closure.
15. Reopen.
16. Feedback submission.
17. Integration error.
18. Access denial events where required.

title: Exception Handling
text:
The system shall handle the following scenarios with clear messages:
1. Mandatory field missing.
2. Invalid order number.
3. Order data not found.
4. Part data not found.
5. Attachment upload failure.
6. Unsupported file type.
7. File size exceeded.
8. API timeout.
9. SAP/ECC data unavailable.
10. Consignment data unavailable.
11. Scan failed.
12. Barcode data incomplete.
13. Unauthorized access.
14. Session expired.
15. Case creation failure.
16. Notification failure.
17. Assignment failure.
18. Closure failure.
19. Feedback submission failure.

title: SAP / API Mismatch Handling
text:
1. Systems shall not show misleading information when SAP/API data is inconsistent.
2. Mismatch should be logged internally.
3. Case be marked as Under Review or Awaiting Backend Update.
4. Support/technical team should analyze whether the issue is from SAP, API, integration,
or application logic.
5. Customers should see only a simple message such as “The latest order information is
being updated.”
6. Incorrect data should not trigger automatic closure without confirmation.

title: Dependencies
text:
The solution depends on:
1. PQMP / EGP API availability.
2. ECC / SAP data availability.
3. Authentication mechanism confirmation.
4. User/dealer/location mapping availability.
5. Notification gateway availability.
6. Attachment storage policy.
7. Final case category and sub-category list.
8. Final status mapping.
9. Final SLA and escalation rules, if applicable.
10. Confirmation of mobile access for support users, if required.
11. Barcode/QR/invoice scan format.
12. Logistics partner API availability.
13. Assignment rule confirmation.
14. Closure rule confirmation.
15. Feedback visibility/reporting confirmation.
16. Email intake scope decision.

title: Key Risks and Mitigation
text:
1. Risk: ECC / SAP data not available in real time.
Mitigation: Show Last Refreshed On and clear fallback messages.
2. Risk: Backend status and quantity not match.
Mitigation: Display Under Review and log mismatch internally.
3. Risk: User access unauthorized cases.
Mitigation: Enforce access control at backend and frontend.
4. Risk: Case creation fail due to integration issue.
Mitigation: Show clear error and preserve entered data.


5. Risk: Notification delivery fail.
Mitigation: Log failed attempts and apply retry policy if approved.
6. Risk: Master data changes affect existing cases.
Mitigation: Audit master changes and preserve historical case values.

title: Out of Scope
text:
The following items are not included in the confirmed current scope unless formally approved:
1. Excel-template-based case creation.
2. Full AI-based case classification.
3. Advanced predictive analytics.
4. Redesign of ECC / SAP transaction screens.
5. Full SAP process automation.
6. Separate escalation management portal integration in Mobile Application
7. CSM Approval workflow.
8. Direct auto closure without business approval and data validation.
9. Full multi-logistics integration unless APIs are made available and confirmed.
10. Any feature not explicitly included in the confirmed functional scope.
